name: Shear
author: E. T. Carter
description: Stratified flow in fast and slow lanes. Stacked horizontal bands stream past one another at alternating speeds, and along every boundary the shear rolls the streamlines up into a marching row of cat-eye billows — the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability, drawn from the exact Stuart-vortex streamfunction. Straight outer streamlines are the lanes; the curled cores are the billows, turning as adjacent rows drift opposite ways.

params.label: Lanes
params.effect: How many shear rows stack up the frame; few gives broad lanes with big rolls, many a finely stratified flow.

params.label: Billows
params.effect: How many cat-eye billows march along each row; few are fat lazy rolls, many a tight rapid train of vortices.

params.label: Roll-up
params.effect: How far the shear rolls the streamlines up; 0 leaves flat parallel lanes, high curls them into fat open cat-eyes.

params.label: Shear speed
params.effect: Drift speed of the lanes (the speed difference driving the shear); 0 freezes the rolls, high streams the lanes briskly past each other.

params.label: Streamlines
params.effect: How many streamlines draw per lane; few are bold ribbons, many a fine layered sheet.

params.label: Line width
params.effect: Thickness of each streamline; fine hairlines to soft broad bands.

params.label: Glow
params.effect: Overall emission of the streamlines; low is a quiet schlieren, high a luminous shear layer.
